:::{#prp-mean-expectation}
#### The mean of numbers is the expectation of one chosen at random

Let $\dsn{a}$ be distinct [real numbers](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/number-systems.html#def-real-numbers),
and let $Y$ be one of them [chosen at random](probability-basics.qmd#def-random-choice).
Then the [expectation](#def-expectation) of $Y$ is the
[mean](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-vectors.html#def-mean) of the numbers:

$$\E{Y} = \avgin a_i$$

:::

::: proof

$$
\ba
\E{Y}
&= \sumin a_i \cd \P(Y = a_i)
&& \text{(definition of expectation; the range of } Y \text{ is } \set{\dsn{a}} \text{)}
\\&= \sumin a_i \cd \frac{1}{n}
&& \text{(each of the } n \text{ numbers is chosen with probability } 1/n \text{)}
\\&= \avgin a_i
&& \text{(definition of the mean)}
\ea
$$

:::
